name: Trust & safety on live-streaming / livestream moderation
category: Adjacent — live moderation of streaming media (video, audio, chat)
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Trust & safety on live-streaming surfaces (live chat, live voice, live video) — per-streamer per-minute report velocity, per-viewer flag rate, per-chat-room message-burst velocity, raid / brigading detection, audio-event flag aggregation, and per-stage / per-game-lobby coordinated-attack signals
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A live-moderation service decides on every chat message, viewer report, voice-toxicity flag, or new joiner — typically within hundreds of milliseconds and never more than a few seconds — whether to slow-mode / ban-evade-throttle / kick / demote-from-stage / shadow-mute / interrupt the livestream, based on per-streamer, per-room, per-viewer and per-(reporter, target) rolling-window features that are seconds-fresh.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Detect hate raids and bot raids in flight: when per-room chat velocity, per-room n_unique(sender_id) and per-room n_unique(account_age_bucket < 24h) all spike simultaneously within a 10–60s sliding window, raise an inline 'raid in progress' signal and trigger automated counter-measures (force followers-only / sub-only / unique-chat / emote-only / suspended-verification) on the channel before the streamer manually reacts. Academic work on Twitch hate raids documents that messages can be sent in under 16 seconds with thousands of unique bot accounts (302 of 1,580 bots sent more than one message in the same raid), so the velocity window must be measured in seconds, not minutes. 2) Quench per-streamer report storms: maintain per-streamer report velocity (count(report, 1m / 5m), n_unique(reporter_id, 5m)) so when a channel is being mass-reported (legitimately or maliciously) the moderation backend can both fast-track human review and detect retaliatory brigade-reporting (high (reporter_id, target_streamer_id) pair counts over 24h/7d). 3) Throttle per-viewer flag abuse: per-viewer flag-rate and n_unique(target_streamer_id, 1h) catch viewers who serial-report many channels (a common harassment vector on Twitch / Kick / TikTok Live). 4) Score per-chat-room message-burst velocity to fire automated slow-mode / sub-only mode: Twitch's existing global '20 messages per 30 seconds for non-mods' and per-channel duplicate-message-drop rules are exactly the shape of features beava would carry, but at the room-aggregate level rather than the per-bot level (the rate-limit gap that hate-raid bots actually exploit). 5) Aggregate per-streamer voice/audio-event flags from upstream classifiers (ToxMod, Hive, Roblox Sentinel, in-house Wav2Vec / Whisper-based detectors) into rolling severity counters and distributions over 30s / 1m / 5m windows, so a single high-severity utterance plus a sustained mid-severity baseline triggers escalation faster than either signal alone. Roblox publishes that voice-related enforcement actions typically occur within 15 seconds, which sets the freshness target. 6) Detect raid / brigading by joins: per-room velocity(viewer_join), n_unique(account_age_bucket<24h, 1m), n_unique(ip_asn, 1m) — sudden floods of newly created accounts from a narrow ASN set within seconds is the canonical pre-raid signature. 7) Per-stage-channel / Discord-stage / Twitter-Space speaker-promotion velocity and demote-rate to detect AMA-hijacking. 8) Feed live-streamer trust scores back into the discovery / recommendation surface so freshly-flagged streamers are downranked within seconds.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events landing in beava as @bv.event: chat_message {ts, room_id (channel_id/stage_id/space_id/lobby_id), sender_id, sender_account_age_s, has_emote, has_link, text_hash, lang, ip_hash, fp, client_kind (web/mobile/embedded), is_subscriber, is_first_message}, viewer_join {ts, room_id, viewer_id, account_age_s, ip_hash, fp, ua_kind, referrer_kind}, viewer_leave {ts, room_id, viewer_id, dwell_ms}, raid_in {ts, source_channel_id, target_channel_id, viewer_count}, follow {ts, viewer_id, target_channel_id}, gift_sub / cheer / donation {ts, viewer_id, target_channel_id, amount_minor, currency}, report {ts, reporter_id, target_id, target_kind (channel|message|stream|user|clip), reason_code, evidence_msg_id?}, voice_flag {ts, room_id, speaker_id, classifier (toxmod|hive|sentinel|internal), category, severity_score, model_version, segment_ms}, mod_action {ts, room_id, moderator_id, target_user_id, action (timeout|ban|delete|kick|demote_from_stage|shadow_mute)}, stage_request {ts, room_id, requester_id}, stage_promote / stage_demote {ts, room_id, target_user_id, mod_id}, clip_create {ts, clip_id, source_channel_id, creator_id, segment_start, segment_len_ms}, stream_start / stream_end. Volume is dominated by chat_message, voice_flag (one per N-second audio segment per active speaker), viewer_join / viewer_leave, and report. Distinct key dimensions to expose as beava entities: room_id, sender_id, target_channel_id, (reporter_id, target_id) pair, (sender_id, room_id) pair, ip_hash, ip_asn, fp, account_age_bucket, clip_id.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Heavy use of beava counter + velocity + n_unique + distribution + distance primitives over very short sliding windows (1s / 5s / 10s / 30s / 1m / 5m / 1h / 24h). Per-room (channel / stage / space / lobby): count(chat_message, 1s/10s/1m), velocity(chat_message), n_unique(sender_id, 10s/1m) (raid-fanout signal), n_unique(account_age_bucket<24h, 1m) (new-account raid signal), n_unique(ip_asn, 1m), n_unique(fp, 1m), distribution(text_hash, 1m) (low entropy = copy-paste bot raid), count(viewer_join, 10s), velocity(viewer_join), count(report, 1m / 5m), n_unique(reporter_id, 5m). Per-streamer (target_channel_id): count(report, 1m/5m/1h), n_unique(reporter_id, 5m/1h) (mass-report signal), distribution(reason_code, 1h), velocity(voice_flag_severity_high), distribution(voice_flag_category, 5m). Per-viewer (viewer_id / reporter_id): count(report, 1h/24h), n_unique(target_channel_id, 1h) (report-spam abuser), count(chat_message, 1m) across all rooms, n_unique(room_id, 5m) (cross-channel raiding individual). Per-(reporter_id, target_channel_id) pair: count(report, 24h/7d) (retaliatory brigading). Per-(sender_id, room_id) pair: count(chat_message, 1m), distribution(text_hash, 5m) (room-spammer detection). Per-IP / per-fp: count(viewer_join, 1m/1h), n_unique(viewer_id, 1h) (sockpuppet fanout), count(account_create, 1h). Per-clip: count(view, 1m), count(report, 1h), velocity(share) (viral-bad-clip detector). Per-stage / Twitter-Space: count(stage_promote, 1m), n_unique(promoted_user_id, 5m), n_unique(demoted_by_self_id, 5m). Distance primitive: per-(viewer_id) geohash distance between successive join events (impossible-travel for account-sharing across regions during a raid). Per-streamer voice severity rolling sum: sum(severity_score, 30s) bucketed by category (harassment / hate / threat / grooming-risk / minor-safety).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Composite and high-cardinality, but with a distinct twist vs. UGC: rooms (room_id / channel_id / stage_id / space_id / lobby_id) are the natural primary aggregation grain because the action surface (slow-mode, followers-only, emote-only, kick) is applied at the room level. Primary keys: room_id, channel_id (= streamer / broadcaster), viewer_id / sender_id / speaker_id, (reporter_id, target_channel_id), (sender_id, room_id), (viewer_id, room_id), ip_hash, ip_asn, fp, account_age_bucket, clip_id. Ephemeral grains: stream_id (lives only for the duration of a broadcast — minutes to hours), stage_session_id, lobby_id. These short-lived grains are a meaningful change from UGC where post_id can live for months: most state in livestream moderation is born and dies within a single broadcast.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate at very short horizons (1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 1m, 5m). Raids ramp in seconds — hate-raid academic data shows thousands of messages in <16 s — so 1–10 s windows are the load-bearing tier. Approximate aggregates (HLL for n_unique(sender_id) and n_unique(reporter_id) per room, CMS for top-K offending senders per room, T-Digest for severity-score distribution) are perfectly acceptable on the high-cardinality axes; 1–3% error is invisible against the moderator's threshold. Session windows tied to the broadcast lifecycle (stream_start / stream_end) are useful because a streamer's audience composition is heavily session-dependent — the moderator wants 'unique chatters in THIS stream' as a session metric, not just 'in the last hour'. Tumbling windows show up for transparency-report aggregation (DSA Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 quantitative templates) and for per-minute timeseries dashboards.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: At-least-once with idempotent counters keyed on event_id is sufficient. Moderation decisions are not money, and during a hate raid duplicate counting biases features in the safe direction (more likely to trip slow-mode / followers-only). Strict no-double-count is required only for regulator transparency reports and for moderator-payable bounty programs (e.g., creator-fund safety incentives at TikTok / YouTube), which are batch-materialized off an event log.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Tighter than UGC because the moderation budget is seconds, not hours. Two operating points. (a) Inline chat / voice path: p99 < 30–50 ms feature-fetch on every chat_message and every voice_flag, because the moderation classifier already runs at sub-second cadence and any added budget directly delays slow-mode / kick action. Roblox reports voice enforcement actions typically within 15 seconds end-to-end, which is the target wall-clock for the whole pipeline including ASR + classifier + feature fetch + action; beava must consume single-digit ms of that. (b) Raid-detection / room-state path: 1–5 s acceptable because the counter-action (force followers-only) only needs to fire within the first 10–30 s of a raid to neuter it. Beava's published sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get fits both budgets with very large headroom.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second to single-digit seconds end-to-end is mandatory. Hate raids complete in under 16 seconds in published academic measurements, so any feature older than 1–2 s is useless for inline raid detection. Voice-flag aggregation requires that a severity_score pushed by the ASR/classifier pipeline appear in the per-streamer rolling sum within hundreds of ms. Beava's push-on-event model with no broker hop fits this strict tier materially better than the Kafka -> Flink -> Redis pipeline most in-house stacks ship today (typical end-to-end freshness 5–30 s). [uncertain]
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly platform-dependent and bursty. Twitch's developer-forum discussions confirm 10,000+ chat messages per second during major live events (e.g., big esports streams), aggregated across all live channels. A single ultra-popular stream might generate ~170 msg/s steady-state, with the long tail of medium streams summing to the bulk of EPS. Roblox processes ~6 billion text chat messages per day (~70k/s sustained, bursting much higher) and ~1.1M hours/day of voice that generates O(10k–100k) voice_flag events per second through ToxMod-style classifiers (1 segment per active speaker every few seconds). Discord public reporting: 4 billion voice-conversation minutes/day. For a single mid-sized buyer (mid-tier livestream platform, mid-tier game studio with voice chat, livestream shopping platform, dating-app live-video, in-app live-audio), sustained ingest is typically 5k–100k EPS with raid bursts to 200k–1M EPS for short windows. A single beava node at the published ~684k EPS (M4, TCP+msgpack, parallel=16) sustained covers all but the largest single-tenant raids; the largest global platforms (Twitch, YouTube Live, TikTok Live, Roblox, Discord) are on a different scale entirely and require horizontal partitioning beava v0 does not yet ship. [uncertain]
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Closer to 1:1 than UGC because most chat_message and voice_flag writes also trigger a synchronous batch_get to score them. Slightly read-heavier (2:1–5:1) during raids because each new viewer_join and each new chat_message also fetches the per-room state to evaluate whether to escalate, and live moderator consoles continuously poll per-streamer feature dashboards.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Smaller and more ephemeral than UGC because most grains die with the stream. A mid-tier livestream platform with ~50k concurrent live channels and ~5M concurrent viewers carries: ~50k active rooms × ~80 counter slots × ~32 B ≈ 130 MB hot room state; ~5M live viewers × ~30 counter slots × ~32 B ≈ 5 GB hot viewer state; per-(reporter, target_channel) pair state for the active broadcast window adds another 1–10 GB depending on report rates. Total typically 10–30 GB live state on a single box, fits comfortably in RAM. A large multi-tenant live-streaming platform (Twitch / YouTube Live / TikTok Live / Bigo / Kick) sees 100k–1M concurrent rooms and 50M+ concurrent viewers, pushing state into the hundreds of GB and exceeding a single beava node. [uncertain]
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Bursty and ephemeral. room_id is bounded by concurrent active streams (10k–1M depending on platform) and resets at stream_end. viewer_id is slowly-growing (MAU plus signup rate). sender_id during a raid is explosive but bounded by the bot fleet size (typically thousands per raid). (reporter_id, target_channel_id) pair is long-tail. clip_id and stream_id are explosive — millions per day on a large platform — but TTL with the broadcast. Approximate aggregates (HLL, CMS, Top-K) are well-fit to the high-cardinality axes during raids.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Aggressive TTLs are mandatory. Hot per-room velocity: 1s–10m sliding windows, evicted at stream_end + grace period (typically 1h to support post-stream review). Per-stream raid features: 5m–1h. Per-viewer cross-channel features: 1h–24h. Per-(reporter, target_channel) pair: 7–30 days for retaliatory-brigading detection. Per-streamer voice-severity rolling sums: 30s–5m for live action, 7–30 days for long-term streamer-risk score. Per-clip state: lifetime of clip virality window (typically 24–72h) then aged out to warehouse. Most state must be evictable on TTL because room_id and clip_id cardinality is unbounded over time.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 10–30 features per inline chat-or-voice-message decision (per-room velocity + per-room unique-sender + per-sender history + per-streamer trust + per-IP / per-ASN reputation + voice-severity rolling sum). Fewer than the UGC writer path because the action surface is even more constrained at room scope (slow-mode / followers-only / sub-only / unique-chat-mode / emote-only / kick), but the per-event rate is much higher, so batch_get throughput matters more than feature count per call.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe. Live moderation decisions are derived state — a node losing its rolling-window during a crash produces seconds of degraded detection, not a regulatory or financial breach (in fact, during a raid the system fails safe by tripping slow-mode on uncertainty). Stream sessions are short-lived (minutes to hours), so even a complete node-loss recovers within one broadcast cycle. DSA / OSA / KOSA transparency-reporting obligations operate periodic-batch off event logs. Beava's WAL + snapshot story comfortably covers the live-moderation durability needs. Note that some regulator-driven retention regimes (DSA 1714 quantitative templates, EU CSAM regulation post-derogation gap) need a separate auditable warehouse for the actual reporting numbers.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Strong fit for single-binary regional or per-PoP sidecar deployments next to the chat ingest service, the WebRTC media path, or the moderation API. Live streaming is inherently regionalized (Twitch / TikTok Live / YouTube Live all run per-region PoPs to minimize end-to-end glass-to-glass latency), and a per-PoP beava sidecar matches that topology naturally. Discord-shard-style architectures (Elixir per-guild sharding) and Twitch's per-channel-server topology also fit single-binary deployment. Multi-region active-active is desired by the largest platforms but not strictly required for a per-region deployment that tolerates a few seconds of replication lag. Hard ceilings: beava v0 has no in-process sharding (a single tenant beyond ~684k EPS or ~100 GB hot state must hand-shard externally — Twitch / Roblox / Discord scale exceeds this); no native multi-tenancy (a vendor like ActiveFence+Modulate or Hive serving many customers needs isolation primitives); refuse-on-network-FS forces local-disk WAL planning per PoP.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Live-streaming Trust & Safety / Integrity / Player Safety / Voice Safety engineering teams at (a) consumer livestream platforms (Twitch, YouTube Live, Kick, TikTok Live, Bigo Live, Whatnot, Niconico, AfreecaTV / SOOP, DLive), (b) social-live-audio platforms (Discord Stage Channels, Twitter/X Spaces, Clubhouse remnants, Spotify Live), (c) gaming companies with in-game voice / in-game text (Activision — Call of Duty, Riot — League / Valorant, Epic — Fortnite, Microsoft — Xbox / Halo, Sony — PlayStation Network, Roblox, EA, Take-Two — Rockstar / 2K, Ubisoft, Nintendo), (d) livestream-commerce platforms (TikTok Shop Live, Amazon Live, Whatnot, Poshmark Live, ShopShops, Bambuser-powered retail livestreams), (e) live-video dating apps (Yubo, MeetMe, LiveMe, Hily live mode, Bumble live), (f) education / kids livestream platforms regulated under KOSA-style frameworks (Outschool live classrooms, Twitch-for-Kids-style products, Roblox education experiences), and (g) live T&S vendors who would embed beava (ActiveFence+Modulate joint offering, Modulate/ToxMod, Hive Moderation Live, Spectrum Labs / Alice live products, Microsoft Community Sift / former Two Hat, Agora-bundled ActiveFence integration, GetStream livestream chat moderation, Lasso, Checkstep live). The buyer is the Live Safety / Voice Safety / Player Safety eng team — distinct from the corporate Risk team, from Growth, and from the static-UGC moderation team (separate org at Twitch / YouTube / TikTok).
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Strong and growth-segment within the broader content-moderation market. The total content-moderation market is ~USD 11.6B in 2025 -> USD 13.3B in 2026 -> USD 26.1B by 2031 at ~14.4% CAGR (Mordor Intelligence). Within that, Live-stream / Voice is advancing at ~18.1% CAGR through 2031 and Gaming-and-Esports at ~16.95% CAGR — both materially faster than the overall market, reflecting regulatory pressure on live media and explosive growth in livestream commerce / live audio. Live-streaming market itself is USD 77–109B in 2025 with 23% CAGR to 2034 (Custom Market Insights, IMARC, Skyquest). Vendor scale: Modulate (ToxMod) is used by Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, RecRoom, and integrated into Discord's Social SDK; ActiveFence + Modulate joint offering covers 100+ languages for video/image/text and 18+ for voice; Agora has bundled ActiveFence moderation into its real-time-engagement SDK (the WebRTC SDK behind many livestream apps); Hive Live is in production at multiple livestream platforms. Roblox publicly reports voice-related abuse reports per DAU cut by ~50% (sources cite both 'cut in half' at GDC and a 15.3% reduction in severe-level reports in the initial rollout). Regulator-driven spend: EU DSA non-compliance fines up to 6% of global turnover (livestream platforms are squarely in scope); UK OSA fines up to 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue (Ofcom has issued >£1M fines and live-streaming-with-minors is an enforcement priority); KOSA-style state-level legislation in CA/UT/NY. [uncertain]
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Regulatory cliff edges with live-streaming as a focal point: EU DSA Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 transparency-report templates (data collection from 1 July 2025, first harmonised reports early 2026) explicitly call out live and ephemeral content; EU Commission's 14 July 2025 guidelines on the protection of minors under the DSA name 'video-sharing sites, gaming environments, and community forums' as in-scope, with age-assurance requirements and bans on targeted ads to children; UK Online Safety Act illegal-harms duties (17 March 2025) and children's-safety duties (25 July 2025) — Ofcom enforcement powers are actively in use as of late 2025 (>£1M fines, 21 investigations) and live-streamed CSAM / grooming is the regulator's top stated priority; voluntary EU CSAM-detection derogation lapsed April 2026 leaving a legal gap forcing platform action; KOSA passed the US Senate in 2024 with bipartisan momentum into 2026 and explicitly covers live features. 2) Real-world harm visibility: Twitch hate raids (2021–2024) put live-chat-flood detection on every safety roadmap; Roblox voice abuse and grooming cases drove Sentinel's open-source release (August 2025) with public claims of catching 35% of cases before user reports during Jan–Jun 2025; Call of Duty's deployment of ToxMod was a public response to community-driven toxicity outcry. 3) AI-driven attack escalation: LLM-generated chat bots can saturate a live chat with semantically diverse spam that defeats text-hash dedup; deepfake voice raids on live audio rooms are an emerging threat. 4) Live commerce growth: TikTok Shop Live, Whatnot, Amazon Live and similar are tying live moderation directly to GMV — a single problematic stream tanks marketplace trust within minutes. 5) Existing tooling pain: in-house teams running Redis + Lua + Flink for chat / voice velocity features publicly complain about ops overhead and the inability to add new features fast enough to keep up with raid evolution.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: EU DSA (Reg. 2022/2065) plus Implementing Regulation 2025/1714 — quantitative templates require transparency reports including action timeliness, which puts pressure on live moderation latency SLOs; live-streaming and ephemeral content are explicitly named. EU Commission guidelines on the protection of minors (14 July 2025) — age assurance, private defaults, ban on targeted ads to children, applies to all live services likely-to-be-used by minors. UK Online Safety Act 2023 — illegal-harms duties (17 March 2025), children's safety duties (25 July 2025), Ofcom enforcement with 10%-of-revenue fines and service-blocking; live-streaming with under-18s is a top enforcement priority. KOSA (US) and state laws (CA AADC, NY SAFE for Kids, UT Social Media Regulation Act). Australian OSA / Singapore OSA / Brazil Marco Civil amendments. GDPR / CCPA — viewer_id, ip_hash, voice biometric markers are personal data; voice transcripts especially require careful retention. SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for platform-buyer procurement. CSAM regimes (US 18 USC 2258A NCMEC reporting; EU CSAM regulation post-derogation; UK CSAM hash-match obligations) — beava is NOT the CSAM hash-match path (PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash for image, audio fingerprinting + Sentinel-style classifiers for live audio) but is the velocity-feature path that complements them. Live-voice biometric data may attract GDPR Art. 9 special-category-data treatment in some jurisdictions, which argues for in-memory only + short TTL (which beava's design accidentally supports). HIPAA only indirectly (telehealth live video).
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: Very fast for the chat-side demo — 1–3 days to a working per-room chat-velocity + per-room unique-sender + raid-detection trigger on beava, since the @bv.event + @bv.table primitives map directly to the Twitch IRC / Discord Gateway / TikTok Live chat event shape. Voice-side integration is 1–2 weeks because it requires an upstream classifier (ToxMod, Hive Voice, Sentinel, internal Whisper-based detector) to push severity_score events into beava. A realistic 20–30-feature production pilot on a mid-sized livestream platform is a 3–8 week effort once auth, TLS, and triggers are added (the v0 gaps below). The 'hate-raid demo' (raid in flight + auto-followers-only + per-room severity heatmap) is the obvious one-page README example for this vertical and is materially more visceral than the static-UGC demo.

competition.incumbents: Generic real-time stack: Redis (counters + Lua, plus Redis Stack with Bloom / CMS / Top-K modules) — every live-platform T&S team interviewed publicly cites Redis as the default for chat rate-limiting and per-room counters; Twitch's per-channel rate-limit buckets are described in dev-forum threads as a token-bucket model. Aerospike at game-platform scale (Roblox, Sony PlayStation Network). Flink / Materialize / RisingWave for buyers with a Kafka backbone wanting SQL semantics. Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk / Fennel as managed online feature stores feeding XGBoost / transformer toxicity / spam models. Custom in-Rust / in-Elixir services on RocksDB / Sled at Discord and Twitch scale. GetStream Chat as a hosted real-time-chat platform with built-in moderation (5M-concurrent-connection benchmark publicly published) — direct competition on the chat-substrate axis. Agora SDK with bundled ActiveFence moderation. Fossabot / Streamer.bot / Nightbot / StreamElements as per-streamer DIY moderation bots running on third-party stacks. Postgres + materialized views at the small end (Bluesky-style federated relays).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: End-to-end live-moderation vendors (the buyer would procure these as black boxes that internally subsume the feature-store layer): Modulate / ToxMod (voice — Call of Duty, RecRoom, Discord Social SDK integration, GDC and AWS case studies), ActiveFence + Modulate joint offering (voice + video + image + text, 100+ languages text / 18+ voice, Agora SDK partnership, Spectrum Labs / Alice product line), Hive AI Moderation (live video and chat moderation, used by Reddit / Bumble / Vimeo and many livestream platforms), Roblox Sentinel (open-sourced August 2025, contrastive-learning grooming-risk classifier — itself an open-source competitor that beava would NOT replace but could complement on the velocity side), Microsoft Community Sift / former Two Hat (Xbox / Azure embedded), Sift Content Integrity (network of 1T events/year), TrustLab (DSA/OSA/AOSA compliance focused, ex-Google/Reddit/ByteDance team), Cinder ('OS for trust & safety', ex-Meta), GetStream Chat with built-in moderation (chat substrate with integrated rate limiting), Agora real-time-engagement SDK with embedded ActiveFence, Lasso (livestream moderation), VoicePatrol, Checkstep (live chat moderation), MediaFirewall (audio moderation). In-house equivalents: Twitch's Safety Engineering team (AutoMod + rate-limit buckets + 'Suspicious User Controls'), YouTube Live Trust & Safety (in-house Google ML stack), TikTok ByteDance live stack, Discord T&S engineering, Roblox Safety Engineering (Sentinel + voice moderation), Activision's player-safety stack, Riot Vanguard / player-safety. Beava would more naturally sit underneath one of these vendors or an in-house team than replace them end-to-end — specifically as the velocity-and-aggregation feature backend that complements an ML classifier from Hive / Modulate / Sentinel.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single binary, no Kafka / Flink / Redis cluster — fits the per-PoP / per-region / per-channel-server sidecar topology that Twitch / Discord / TikTok Live actually deploy. 2) 50+ aggregation primitives natively cover the velocity / n_unique / distribution / distance features live moderation lives on, without writing Lua scripts or Flink SQL — addresses the Redis+Lua maintenance burden that Twitch and Discord teams publicly cite, and lets safety engineers iterate features in Python at @bv.event speed rather than redeploying Flink jobs. 3) Sub-ms TCP+msgpack get / batch_get matches the inline chat-message and voice-flag latency budget — the critical seconds-budget of live moderation. Roblox's 15-second-end-to-end voice-action SLO is achievable with beava-level feature latency but tight with Redis+Lua at scale. 4) Apache-2.0, no open-core — attractive to live-T&S vendors (Modulate, Hive, ActiveFence, Cinder) who want to embed it rather than depend on a competitor's managed cloud, and attractive to large in-house teams (Twitch, Discord, Roblox, Activision) who do not want vendor lock-in on integrity-critical infrastructure. 5) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed TCP, msgpack) maps directly to how chat ingest, WebRTC media paths, and voice-classifier sidecars already shape events; no broker hop. 6) Distance primitive cleanly expresses impossible-travel signals for account-sharing across regions during a coordinated raid. 7) Native (sender_id, room_id) and (reporter_id, target_channel_id) composite-key tables let raid-detection and retaliatory-reporting features be expressed as first-class, which Redis requires hand-rolled hash-of-hash schemes for. 8) In-memory + WAL + refuse-on-network-FS is accidentally well-aligned with the regulatory pressure to short-TTL voice biometric data (GDPR Art. 9). 9) The ephemeral-grain shape (stream_id, lobby_id, stage_session_id born and dying with the broadcast) plus TTL eviction maps naturally to the live-moderation lifecycle in a way that batch-feature-stores (Tecton / Hopsworks / Chalk) do not.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS, no auth in v0 on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 — disqualifying for any production deployment by a regulated live platform; effectively limits beava today to in-VPC / behind-mTLS-proxy deployments. SOC 2 / DSA / OSA / KOSA audit programs all require authenticated access to integrity infrastructure. 2) No in-process sharding — Twitch / YouTube Live / TikTok Live / Roblox / Discord scale exceeds a single box at ~684k EPS / ~100 GB hot state; raid bursts can briefly push a single channel-server beyond a single node. 3) Refuse-on-network-FS plus in-memory-only means buyers must plan local-disk WAL and bound cold-start replay time; a node restart during an active hate raid is an outage when seconds count. 4) No triggers / 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — live moderation is inherently event-driven ('when (room_id).unique_sender_count_1m crosses N AND new_account_pct crosses M, auto-enable followers-only', 'when (streamer).voice_severity_sum_30s crosses S, alert SOC and queue review'), and polling 10–30 features on every chat_message just to threshold them is wasteful at livestream EPS. This is the most-cited workflow gap. 5) No multi-tenancy primitives — a live-T&S-as-a-service vendor (Modulate, Hive, ActiveFence, Lasso, Checkstep) serving many customers needs per-tenant namespaces, quotas, rate-limit accounting, and cross-tenant isolation. 6) No secondary indexes / no 'list all live rooms with unique-sender-velocity > X in last 10s' query — kills the live-SOC dashboard surface; Twitch / Discord / Roblox internal live-T&S consoles expose exactly this view. 7) No native graph / pair-clustering primitives for coordinated raid detection (Meta CIB-style URL-sharing time-similarity graphs, account-cluster signatures shared across raid platforms). 8) No CSAM / PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash / audio-fingerprint integration — orthogonal but buyers expect a documented sidecar story. 9) No native PII / voice-biometric handling story (ip_hashing at rest, configurable retention windows, right-to-erasure cascading, voice-fingerprint salting) — GDPR Art. 9 / DSA / KOSA / CA AADC make this load-bearing. 10) No native streaming consumption / change-data-capture out (e.g., to feed a downstream warehouse for DSA 1714 quantitative reports) — buyers will need a sidecar to materialise the counters. 11) Single-binary refuses-network-FS means per-PoP planning is required; live-streaming buyers run dozens of PoPs and operational tooling for fleet management is on the buyer.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: chat ingest service (Twitch IRC / TMI, Discord Gateway, TikTok Live WebSocket, YouTube Live Chat API, Kick chat, Bigo chat — all push chat_message events at sub-second cadence), WebRTC media plane and voice classifier sidecars (Modulate ToxMod, Hive Voice, Roblox Sentinel, in-house Whisper-based detectors push voice_flag events per N-second segment per speaker), viewer-presence service (viewer_join / viewer_leave events from the streaming media gateway), report endpoint (one HTTP POST per viewer report), federation-style or partner-streamed events (Agora SDK with bundled moderation, GetStream Chat push events). Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 fits the application-server-and-webhook producer; TCP+msgpack :8081 fits high-throughput chat / voice gateways during raids. Consumers: rules engines (AutoMod-style YAML, Twitch's 'Suspicious User Controls' configuration, in-house Drools / FEEL, Cinder workflow engine), ML scorers (XGBoost / LightGBM for spam and abuse, transformer-based toxicity models like Perspective, Hive content moderation suite, Roblox Sentinel grooming-risk classifier, Modulate ToxMod), and inline action surface in the chat-server / media-plane (slow-mode, followers-only, sub-only, unique-chat, emote-only, kick, demote-from-stage, timeout, ban-evade-throttle).
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both, with a heavier deterministic-rules tilt than UGC because slow-mode / followers-only / sub-only need to fire on simple, explainable thresholds in seconds. Buyers run deterministic per-room rules (Twitch-style 'if room_chat_velocity_10s > N AND new_account_pct > M then auto-followers-only', AutoMod YAML, in-house DSL) alongside ML scorers (toxicity transformers, grooming-risk classifiers like Sentinel, voice-toxicity models like ToxMod). Beava as a pure feature backend stays decoupled from the scorer — both the rules engine and the ML model read from the same batch_get path.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No public users of beava on this use case yet. [uncertain] Comparable production systems and published case studies that legitimize the shape of the problem: Roblox open-sourced Sentinel (August 2025) — contrastive-learning grooming-risk classifier with 256-tick context windows, ~1,200 NCMEC reports submitted Jan–Jun 2025, 35% of cases caught before user reports; Roblox public reporting on voice moderation deployed across 31 countries with abuse-reports-per-active-hour cut in half (GDC talk) and 15.3% reduction in severe-level voice abuse reports + 11.4% decrease in violations per minute in the initial rollout; Modulate ToxMod publicly deployed at Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, RecRoom, integrated into Discord's Social SDK; ActiveFence + Modulate joint offering with Agora's WebRTC SDK; academic papers on Twitch hate raids (Han et al., CSCW 2023, arXiv 2305.16248 — 'thousands of messages in under 16 seconds', 1,580 bots per raid measured); Discord public reporting on 4 billion voice-conversation minutes/day with harassment as 32% of incident reports; GetStream Chat's published 5M-concurrent-connection benchmark for chat substrate; Twitch developer-forum threads on 10,000+ chat messages/second during major live events and TMI token-bucket rate limits (20 msgs / 30s for non-mods, 50 msgs / 30s for known bots); ActiveFence + Agora partnership (2023) on real-time-engagement moderation; Hive Moderation public dashboards for livestream platforms.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: No beava-specific Discord / GitHub Discussion threads on livestream T&S use cases located yet. [uncertain] Broader community is highly active: Twitch dev forums (discuss.dev.twitch.com — rate-limit and hate-raid threads), Discord engineering blog and community-moderation forums, Roblox DevForum (voice chat moderation, Sentinel rollout), Hacker News threads on Roblox Sentinel open-sourcing (August 2025) and on Twitch hate raids, TrustCon and GDC Trust & Safety tracks, Integrity Institute community, Modulate / ToxMod webinars and AWS-for-Games blog series, Agora developer community on ActiveFence moderation integration, academic CSCW / CHI tracks on livestream moderation (papers by Jie Cai and collaborators on categorizing live-streaming moderation tools).
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: No dedicated livestream / chat-raid / voice-severity-aggregation demo identified in the beava repository as of the snapshot reviewed. The closest analogues are the generic fraud demo (python/beava/demos/fraud, events.jsonl + schema.json) and the e-commerce demo (python/beava/demos/ecommerce). A natural addition would be examples/livestream_moderation with chat_message / viewer_join / report / voice_flag events keyed on room_id, sender_id, streamer_id, (reporter_id, target_channel_id), demonstrating raid detection (room velocity spike + new-account fraction + IP-ASN concentration), per-streamer voice-severity rolling sum, and per-viewer cross-channel report-abuse detection. [uncertain]
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Maximum — among the most actively adversarial domains in tech. Hate raids retool weekly (residential-proxy bot networks, LLM-generated semantically-diverse chat spam, deepfake voice raids on audio rooms, coordinated cross-platform raid planning on Telegram and Discord). The seconds-budget makes feature-drift especially expensive — by the time a static feature is shipped through a Flink-deploy pipeline, attackers have already adapted. This strongly argues for a developer-ergonomic feature backend (beava's @bv.event / @bv.table model) over a SQL-on-Flink pipeline that requires schema-migration to add a new counter. Roblox's published 'cut voice abuse in half' result followed dedicated infra investment in real-time multimodal review; the regulatory ratchet (DSA 1714, OSA, KOSA) plus livestream-commerce GMV exposure intensifies the arms race.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) CSAM / NCMEC hash matching itself — PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash / Thorn Safer for image and video, and audio-fingerprinting + content-classifier sidecars for live audio; beava can complement those by counting per-uploader / per-streamer CSAM-hit velocity but cannot replace them. 2) NLP / toxicity / grooming-risk classification on raw text or audio — that belongs in Hive / Perspective / Modulate ToxMod / Roblox Sentinel / in-house transformer models, not beava. 3) ASR / speech-to-text — Whisper / wav2vec / cloud STT belongs upstream; beava consumes voice_flag events emitted by the classifier. 4) Long historical lookback for transparency reports (DSA 1714 quantitative templates require multi-month aggregates) — beava is in-memory; reporting belongs in Parquet / a lakehouse. 5) Cross-entity graph clustering for coordinated raid detection — beava has no join engine; that's a graph-DB / OLAP problem, although beava can serve per-cluster aggregates once a cluster_id is computed externally. 6) Full event archive / forensic case review of every chat_message and every voice segment — WAL is for crash recovery, not analyst case exploration; that needs an event log + warehouse. 7) Acting as the rules engine, the ML scorer, or the moderation UI — beava is the feature backend, not the moderation product. 8) Strict regulator-grade durability for transparency reports — beava can do crash-safe live features but the reported numbers should be sourced from an auditable warehouse. 9) Multi-region active-active in v0. 10) Voice / audio raw-storage — voice biometric raw audio is GDPR Art. 9 special-category data and should never sit in beava's hot state; only derived severity scores should.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for livestream moderation, roughly in priority order: 1) TLS termination and mutual TLS on :8080 / :8081 / :8090 plus an auth model (token, mTLS, or both) on push and admin surfaces — without this, no regulated live platform (DSA / OSA / KOSA exposure) or live-T&S-as-a-service vendor can deploy externally; this is the same blocker as the UGC and bot-defence verticals and the single most important gap. 2) Triggers / 'fire callback when (room_id).unique_sender_count_10s crosses N' — live moderation is fundamentally event-driven and seconds-budgeted (auto-followers-only on raid detection, demote-from-stage on speaker-promotion velocity spike, kick on per-sender chat velocity, alert SOC, force unique-chat-mode), and polling 10–30 features on every chat_message at livestream EPS just to threshold them is wasteful at hundreds-of-thousands of messages per second. This is the single most-cited workflow gap and is materially more important here than in UGC because the seconds budget is harder. 3) HLL / Bloom / CMS / Top-K approximate primitives as first-class aggregations on per-room sender_id, ip_asn, fp axes to keep cardinality bounded during raids; if these are already in the 50+ primitives, document them prominently with a worked 'top-K offending senders in last 10 seconds during a raid' example. 4) In-process or sidecar sharding by key prefix (room_id, channel_id, ip_asn) so livestream platforms beyond ~684k EPS / ~100 GB can scale within one cluster without external hand-sharding. 5) Per-key TTL / sliding-window eviction tied to broadcast lifecycle (stream_start / stream_end events should be able to cascade-evict per-stream state) so explosive room_id / clip_id cardinality during high-traffic windows doesn't OOM the box. 6) Session-window primitive (broadcast = session) for 'unique chatters in THIS stream' rather than 'in the last hour' — distinct from sliding-window semantics and a load-bearing concept for live moderation that isn't naturally a tumbling or sliding window. 7) Multi-tenancy: per-tenant namespaces, quotas, per-tenant rate-limit accounting for vendors serving many customers (Modulate, Hive, ActiveFence, Lasso, Checkstep, Agora-bundled offerings). 8) Streaming admin / debug surface and secondary indexes so live SOC analysts can run 'top-K rooms by chat velocity in last 10 seconds' or 'top-K streamers by voice-severity sum in last 30s' without materializing the whole keyspace — Twitch / Discord / Roblox / TikTok internal live-T&S consoles expose this view today. 9) Native PII / voice-biometric handling: ip / fingerprint hashing at rest, configurable per-namespace retention, right-to-erasure that cascades through all derived aggregates (GDPR Art. 17, especially Art. 9 for voice biometrics, DSA Art. 14, KOSA-aligned state laws, CA AADC). 10) Composite-key (pair / triple) aggregations as first-class — (sender, room), (reporter, target_channel), (viewer, room), (ip_asn, account_age_bucket) — these are the natural live-moderation grains and need to be ergonomic in @bv.table. 11) Documented hooks for graph-cluster enrichment (external CIB / raid-coordination clustering job pushes cluster_id sidecar into beava). 12) Cold-start strategy: WAL replay time on a node with tens of GB of hot room / streamer state must be benchmarked and bounded; otherwise a restart during an active hate raid is an outage. 13) CSAM / hash-match / live-CSAM detection integration pattern documented (sidecar to PhotoDNA / PDQ / NeuralHash for image, audio-fingerprint or live-classifier for audio, with beava counting per-uploader / per-streamer hit velocity). 14) Reference architecture published for DSA 1714 / OSA / KOSA: warehouse for transparency reports + beava for live counters + classifier sidecar (Hive / Modulate / Sentinel) — buyers want an opinionated stack diagram. 15) Native push-based change-data-capture out of beava so per-minute / per-second timeseries can stream to a downstream Prometheus / OpenTelemetry / warehouse without buyers building their own polling adapter. 16) Per-stream session lifecycle hooks (on stream_start / stream_end) for state lifecycle automation.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — even more strongly than in static UGC. Live moderation is fundamentally event-driven and operates on a seconds budget: 'when (room).unique_sender_count_10s crosses N AND new_account_pct_1m crosses M, auto-enable followers-only-mode'; 'when (streamer).voice_severity_sum_30s crosses S, page on-call and queue human review'; 'when (room).chat_velocity_5s crosses V, trip slow-mode'; 'when (viewer).reports_filed_1h crosses R across N distinct channels, throttle reporting privileges'. Polling 10–30 features on every chat_message at livestream EPS just to threshold them is wasteful, latency-eating, and operationally fragile. Triggers are the most-cited gap for this domain alongside TLS + auth, and arguably the bigger blocker for the live-T&S vertical specifically because the action surface is so tightly coupled to threshold-crossing semantics.
